key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Acute, often following myocardial infarction (MI) or acute heart failure. LOCATION: Generalized, systemic hypoperfusion. DURATION: Continuous, life-threatening. CHARACTER: Severe dyspnea, chest pain (if myocardial infarction ), altered mental status, cold/clammy skin. AGGRAVATING: Reduced cardiac output. RELIEVING: Inotropic support, revascularization. TIMING: Acute decompensation. SEVERITY: Critical, life-threatening. KEY POSITIVES: Hypotension (systolic blood pressure (SBP) <90 mmHg), tachycardia, cold clammy extremities, altered mental status, oliguria (low urine output), pulmonary edema, recent myocardial infarction (MI), severe heart failure. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT septic shock (warm extremities), NOT hypovolemic shock (responds to fluids).

red_flags: Recent myocardial infarction (MI) or severe heart failure
